questions.prompt: By default (no scheduler, no time operator), how does `of(1, 2, 3)` emit?

options.text: Synchronously — it emits immediately and blocks

questions.explanation: RxJS is synchronous by default. of/from emit immediately. Asynchrony only appears when a scheduler or time-based operator is involved.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `observeOn` and `subscribeOn`?

options.text: observeOn reschedules downstream delivery of notifications; subscribeOn reschedules when the subscription (producer start) runs
observeOn starts the producer; subscribeOn delivers values

questions.explanation: observeOn moves each notification's delivery onto a scheduler from its position downstream. subscribeOn schedules the whole subscription (the producer start), applied once wherever it sits.

questions.prompt: Which scheduler schedules work on the microtask queue, running before timers and rendering?
questions.explanation: asapScheduler uses the Promise/microtask queue. asyncScheduler uses macrotasks (setTimeout-style).

questions.prompt: Which scheduler is best for driving an animation?

options.text: animationFrameScheduler — it aligns emissions with requestAnimationFrame

questions.explanation: animationFrameScheduler schedules via requestAnimationFrame, so updates happen once per paint — smooth and efficient, without wasted work between frames.

questions.prompt: Passing a scheduler to of/from/range is deprecated. Type the function you use instead: `__________([1,2,3], asyncScheduler)`.
questions.explanation: scheduled(input, scheduler) is the modern way to create an Observable that emits its input on a given scheduler.

questions.prompt: Match each scheduler to its mechanism.
questions.explanation: async = macrotask, asap = microtask, queue = synchronous with trampolining for safe recursion, animationFrame = paint-synced via rAF.
